CLINICAL DOCUMENTATION — NARRATIVE SURGICAL DISCHARGE SUMMARY V1
Patient: Joseph Taylor | MRN: PAT-60015 | DOB: 1964-12-07 | Gender: Male | Doc ID: NARRATIVE_0015
Encounter Date: 2025-05-24 | Discharge/Note Date: 2025-05-29 | Provider: Dr. Lisa Cuddy, MD
PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS & PROCEDURE
The patient underwent uncomplicated arthroscopic knee meniscectomy and chondroplasty under general endotracheal
anesthesia.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
The patient is an adult who presented electively for surgical intervention following conservative management failure.
Pre-admission testing confirmed that preoperative total cholesterol was 235.6 mg/dL (HIGH). Preoperative metabolic
screening showed a baseline platelet count of 521 10*3/uL (HIGH). The patient was cleared from a cardiopulmonary
standpoint and taken to the operative suite.
POSTOPERATIVE HOSPITAL COURSE
The patient was extubated in the operating room and transferred to the post-anesthesia care unit in stable condition.
Postoperative recovery was uneventful. For pain and infection prophylaxis, the patient was prescribed Amlodipine 5 mg
orally once daily. On postoperative day one, postoperative creatinine remained stable at 0.92 mg/dL. Surgical incisions were
clean, intact, and without erythema or purulent drainage.
POST-DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS
Discharge medications: The patient will take Amoxicillin 250 mg by mouth three times daily for 7 days, and continue
baseline Omeprazole 40 mg orally once daily in the morning for 30 days. All prescriptions were transmitted electronically to
the patient's pharmacy.
ACTIVITY & WOUND CARE PLAN
Keep dressing clean and dry. No heavy lifting greater than 10 pounds for two weeks. Surgical clinic follow-up scheduled in
10 days.
